item.title: ‘Nigerians mocked me but they understand now’ – Patience Jonathan on Chibok girls
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Former First Lady, Dame Patience Jonathan, has revisited the controversy surrounding her emotional reaction to the abduction of schoolgirls from Chibok, Borno State, in 2014, saying Nigerians who mocked her at the time are only now beginning to understand the pain she experienced. Jonathan said the incident remained deeply painful to her because she regarded the abducted girls as her own children. She recalled breaking down in tears when she learnt of their abduction and said the memory still affected her more than a decade later. The former First Lady spoke during an interview with the Nigerian Television Authority on Saturday, where she expressed disappointment over the public ridicule she faced following her emotional response to the tragedy. “I remember 2014. I broke down. I am still feeling it as I talk to you. They are my children. But people started laughing and mocking me. I felt bad. People laughing at me have no empathy. It is today they are realising what happened to me at that time. It still pains me,” she said. Her remarks revisit one of the most controversial moments of her time as First Lady, when she was criticised and widely mocked after breaking down during a meeting with parents and other stakeholders over the abduction. On the night of April 14, 2014, Boko Haram insurgents abducted 276 schoolgirls from Government Girls Secondary School in Chibok, Borno State. The incident triggered international outrage and the #BringBackOurGirls campaign, drawing attention to the security crisis in Nigeria’s North-East. Jonathan’s emotional reaction became a subject of public discussion, with some Nigerians questioning her response to the tragedy. However, in her latest comments, she said those who laughed at her lacked empathy and had failed to appreciate what she was going through at the time. item.title: Adebule ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​⁠⁠​​​⁠‌​for burial Sunday as Lagos APC suspends campaign activities
item.description: The remains of Sen. Idiat Adebule, former deputy governor of Lagos State, will be buried on Sunday, Nov. 29, at Ebony Vaults and Gardens, Ikoyi, Lagos. The burial ceremony is scheduled for 3 p.m., according to a statement issued on Saturday by Mr. Seye Oladejo, All Progressives Congress (APC) spokesman in Lagos. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Adebule, who until her death was representing Lagos West Senatorial District in the National Assembly, died on Saturday at 56. Oladejo said the party called on its leaders, elected representatives, stakeholders, members, and supporters to attend the burial and pay their last respects to the deceased senator. He described Adebule, who represented Lagos West Senatorial District, as a political leader, educationist, and distinguished public servant whose sudden death had plunged the party into deep mourning. “Her years of service, commitment to the progressive ideals of the APC and contributions to the political and developmental advancement of Lagos State will remain indelible,” he said. Oladejo said the senator’s death represented a painful and irreplaceable loss to the party and the entire Lagos political family. Meanwhile, the Director-General of the Lagos State APC PBAT/KOH Campaign Council, Sen. Musiliu Obanikoro, has announced the suspension of all campaign activities of the council until further notice. According to Oladejo, the decision was taken as the party mourned the late senator and reflected the profound grief within its ranks. He said the suspension was necessary to accord the deceased the honor, dignity, and solemnity befitting her stature and contributions to public service. “The Lagos APC leadership urges all campaign structures, directorates, committees, supporters, and stakeholders to respect this directive as we collectively mourn this painful loss and stand in solidarity with her family,” he said. Oladejo said the party also extended its condolences to Adebule’s immediate family, political associates, constituents, and the entire Lagos West Senatorial District. He prayed that Almighty Allah would grant her soul eternal rest and give those she left behind the strength to bear the loss. “Adieu, Distinguished Sen. Idiat Adebule. Your service will not be forgotten,” he said. (NAN) The post Adebule ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​⁠⁠​​​⁠‌​for burial Sunday as Lagos APC suspends campaign activities appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Adebule To Be Buried Sunday As Lagos APC Suspends Campaign Activities
item.description: The remains of former Lagos State Deputy Governor and Senator representing Lagos West, Idiat Oluranti Adebule, will be buried on Sunday, November 29, at the Ebony Vaults and Gardens, Ikoyi, Lagos. Adebule died on Saturday in Lagos at the age of 56, following a brief illness, barely a day after celebrating her birthday. The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) announced her burial date in a statement issued on Saturday by its spokesperson, Seye Oladejo. According to the statement, the burial will take place at 3 p.m., with party leaders, elected representatives, stakeholders, members and supporters expected to attend. The APC flag The party described Adebule’s death as a painful loss, saying her contributions to public service and the development of Lagos State would remain indelible. Meanwhile, the Director-General of the Lagos State APC PBAT/KOH Campaign Council, Musiliu Obanikoro, has announced the suspension of all campaign activities until further notice in honour of the deceased senator. The party said the decision was taken to reflect the grief within its ranks and accord Adebule the dignity befitting her contributions to public service. It urged all campaign structures, directorates, committees, supporters and stakeholders to comply with the directive. Tributes Senate President Godswill Akpabio and President Bola Tinubu. Her death has attracted tributes from President Bola Tinubu, Senate President Godswill Akpabio and Lagos State Deputy Governor Kadri Hamzat, among other political leaders. Tinubu expressed shock and sadness over her death in a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga. The President described her passing as a painful loss to Lagos State, the National Assembly and the country, recalling her contributions to governance, education and public administration. Similarly, Akpabio described Adebule as a treasured colleague and accomplished administrator. In a condolence message issued through his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Eseme Eyiboh, he said, “It is with a heavy heart and an overwhelming sense of grief that I received the devastating news of the passing of our distinguished colleague, Senator Idiat Oluranti Adebule.” File photo of Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hamzat. Hamzat also described the late senator as a dedicated public servant and accomplished educationist. “I am deeply saddened by the passing of my sister and predecessor in office, Senator Idiat Oluranti Adebule. She served Lagos State with distinction as Deputy Governor and continued that service with commitment as Senator representing Lagos West,” he said. He added that she was “a woman of peace, integrity and compassion, who touched many lives through education and public service.” Senator Idiat Adebule died in Lagos a day after her 56th birthday Adebule was born on November 27, 1970, in Ojo, Lagos State. item.title: NPFL : Shooting Stars hit with N5m fine, banned from home stadium
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Nigeria Premier Football League has fined Shooting Stars Sports Club N5m and ordered the team to relocate its home matches to Owerri indefinitely following crowd trouble after their encounter with Rivers United in Ibadan. The league announced the sanctions in a statement published on its official website on Saturday, November 28, 2026, following Friday’s incident at the Lekan Salami Stadium. According to the NPFL, the Ibadan based club failed to provide adequate security, resulting in the compromise of the safety of the visiting team, match officials and other participants. The league also accused Shooting Stars supporters of encroaching into restricted areas and onto the field of play before holding the referees and Rivers United contingent hostage for 35 minutes after the match. It further alleged that some supporters attempted to assault the match officials and members of the visiting team. Consequently, the NPFL ordered Shooting Stars to play their home fixtures at the Dan Anyiam Stadium in Owerri, Imo State, indefinitely, while the Lekan Salami Stadium will no longer host the club’s league matches. The N5m fine was imposed for repeated failure to provide adequate security, encroachment onto the pitch, attempted assault on match officials and holding the referees and visiting team hostage after the encounter. In another development, the league recommended that the referees who officiated the match be delisted from the competition. The NPFL explained that the contents of the match officials’ report indicated that they were not assaulted, a situation which left the league body handicapped in its handling of the incident. The governing body also warned Shooting Stars and other clubs against attacking, harassing or obstructing crew members of its broadcast partner, stressing that such conduct would attract stiff sanctions. The disciplinary measures followed Friday’s encounter between Shooting Stars and Rivers United at the Lekan Salami Stadium, which ended in a draw. item.title: ‘It’s difficult to be positive’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 0-4 defeat
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino has admitted that it is difficult to remain positive after his side suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday. Pochettino, who was overseeing his first home match as United manager, expressed disappointment with the result but urged his players to remain united and work together to turn around the club’s fortunes. Speaking after the encounter at Old Trafford, the Argentine said United started the match strongly but struggled after conceding the opening goal. “Difficult to be positive. Very disappointed, disappointed at the same time because I feel sorry for the players,” he said. “The players from the beginning, during 15 to 20 minutes, we were very solid, organisation, structure. I think we were controlling the game. The moment we concede the goal, we should not concede this goal.” Callum Wilson scored twice in the first half to put Brentford in control before Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade added two more goals in the closing stages to complete the visitors’ victory. Pochettino admitted that conceding the first goal affected his players’ confidence and made the contest more difficult for them. He insisted that the squad must remain calm despite the difficult situation, adding that he believes the team will improve with time. “The game goes difficult, the intensity, the nerves. This situation, a situation like this, is affecting your confidence, but we need to be united and stay together and keep pushing. “We are going to push to improve and, of course, it is only a matter of time that we are going to improve. We need to stay together, we need to stay calm. That is why we’re here. We have the responsibility to turn this situation into another way,” he added. Asked whether the challenge at Manchester United had been bigger than he initially anticipated, Pochettino said he knew the club was going through difficult circumstances before accepting the job. The former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur manager explained that the team’s busy fixture schedule had also made it difficult to implement his ideas, particularly with three matches played within 10 days. “No, we knew it was going to be bigger. That is why we are here. No change in my view. Only that things need time to change in football more. When the fixtures and schedule is so busy,” he said. He added that the players had remained receptive to his instructions and were making efforts to improve despite the disappointing results. “The reaction of the players when we lost 4-0. They tried and they care. That is the most important thing. We need to feel the pain and increase our standards and try to do anything to be much better.” The defeat extended United’s winless run in the Premier League to 10 matches, their longest such streak since going 11 games without a victory between November 1989 and February 1990. item.title: Why I pursued master’s degree while still playing football – Oshoala
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Super Falcons forward Asisat Oshoala has explained that her desire to prepare for life beyond professional football motivated her decision to pursue a Master’s degree in International Sports Management. Oshoala, who recently graduated from the Global Institute of Sport (GIS), said she considered furthering her education important because she intends to remain active in the sporting sector even after her playing career. The six time African Women’s Player of the Year disclosed this in an interview at the Super Falcons’ training camp ahead of their international friendly matches against Algeria. Explaining her decision to return to the classroom, the 32 year old said she wanted to start thinking about her future and other opportunities outside playing football. “I felt like I needed to start thinking about other things, what I want to do in the future, so I needed to study. I own a club and I still want to be in the sporting sector, so it is a good thing to study,” she said. The former Barcelona forward stressed that education would not be a wasted investment, particularly for people who have genuine interests in their chosen fields. She also encouraged professional footballers to make use of the time available to them outside training and matches to develop themselves academically and acquire additional skills. According to her, although footballers dedicate several hours daily to training, they still have enough time to pursue other interests and invest in their personal development. “As a footballer, you know you have like 24 hours in a day, but you have like two or four to six hours to train, so you can use other hours to invest in yourself,” she added. Oshoala’s comments come days after she celebrated her graduation with an MSc in International Sports Management, adding an academic qualification to a football career that has brought her several individual and team honours. Her latest achievement reflects her intention to build a future within the sports industry beyond her exploits on the pitch. The Nigerian international has won the African Women’s Player of the Year award a record six times and lifted four Women’s Africa Cup of Nations titles with the Super Falcons The post Why I pursued master’s degree while still playing football – Oshoala appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC mock polls record large turnouts in Edo, Osun, Nasarawa; ‘We’re satisfied’ – INEC
item.description: *… BVAS worked smoothly in Abuja *We’re satisfied – INEC By Omeiza Ajayi, Ozioruva Aliu, Shina Abubakar & Edwin Philip The residents of Edo, Osun and Nasarawa states turned out massively on Saturday for the mock election exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, in the designated polling units nationwide. Meanwhile, the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, devices deployed for the nationwide mock presidential election worked smoothly at polling units in Kubwa and Garki. Voters at the Garki unit accredited in less than one minute each. At the City Centre Polling Unit by Area 10, Garki Post Office, in the Abuja Municipal Area Council, AMAC, 18 persons were accredited successfully. Each of them was accredited individually in less than one minute. Three BVAS devices were deployed in the unit. At Polling Unit 024 (PU024), Arab Road/Water Board Junction in Kubwa, Bwari Area Council, the BVAS devices also worked well. Few voters were seen trickling in at intervals. At the Gbazango Garina Hausawa polling unit in Kubwa, INEC officials said they were still waiting for voters hours after opening of poll. There were also a gew voters at Phase 3, by the Model School in Kubwa. Edo State In Benin City, Edo State capital, a visit to Ward 7, Unit 42, New Benin, in Oredo Local Government Area of the state showed an impressive turnout of voters, who came out to participate in the exercise. Speaking with journalists, Mr Daniel Odenigbo, an All Progressives Congress, APC, party agent, described the exercise as peaceful and orderly, commending INEC officials for their efficiency. Odenigbo said the turnout was encouraging, adding that voters were cooperating with the electoral officials to ensure a smooth process. Similarly, a visit to Ward 6 in the same local government area also revealed an encouraging turnout of participants. Speaking with journalists, the APC Ward 6 Chairman in Oredo, Christopher Ize, described the turnout as impressive, expressing optimism that more people would participate as the exercise progressed. Osun Also, in some polling units in Osun State, INEC mock test for the reliability of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, ahead of the 2027 general elections, witnessed good turnout. In most of the polling units visited by Vanguard, the BVAS worked perfectly on facial recognition, while the fingerprints recorded low recognition. The facial recognition takes about 30-40 seconds to recognized voter’s faces after which a dummy ballot is handed to the voter to cast a vote with the process taking about one to two minutes. item.title: ‎Tinubu mourns former Lagos deputy gov, Senator Idiat Adebule
item.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja President Bola Tinubu has expressed profound shock and sadness over the sudden passing of former Lagos State Deputy Governor and incumbent Senator representing Lagos West, Senator Idiat Oluranti Adebule. ‎Adebule, 56, died after a brief illness in Lagos. ‎President Tinubu described her death as a painful loss not only to Lagos State and the National Assembly but to the nation as a whole, particularly at a time when her experience, commitment, and contributions to public service are needed. ‎The President recalled the lawmaker’s distinguished record of service and her tenure as Deputy Governor (2015-2019), during which she worked to advance governance and development in the state. ‎He noted the deceased’s political journey, which reflects years of commitment to public administration, education, and empowering citizens, particularly women and the youth. The president lauded her legislative contributions, noting that she continued to demonstrate dedication to democratic governance and the representation of her constituents. President Tinubu extended his heartfelt condolences to her immediate family, the government and people of Lagos State, political associates, members of the All Progressives Congress (APC), the National Assembly, and all those mourning her passing. ‎He prayed that Almighty Allah grant her Aljannatul Firdaus and give her family, friends, and associates the strength to bear this irreparable loss. ‎ ‎ The post ‎Tinubu mourns former Lagos deputy gov, Senator Idiat Adebule appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Netanyahu offers to rotate Israeli premiership with Eisenkot
item.description: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday proposed a rotating premiership with his main rival Gadi Eisenkot, who would go first, with the latter expected to announce the formation of a new government within days. Proposing a unity government in a social media post, Netanyahu said “my responsibility as a leader requires me to set everything aside… and agree that Gadi Eisenkot will serve first as prime minister, while I will serve as alternate prime minister at the beginning of the term”. The offer came one day after Eisenkot vowed to announce the formation of Israel’s next government by the official deadline of December 6, without using the option of a 14-day extension. He is expected to form a coalition with anti-Netanyahu parties, but his centrist Yashar party has also been conducting negotiations with Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud. On Friday, however, Eisenkot accused Likud of stalling coalition talks in a bid to bring about new elections. “Likud… has been unwilling to compromise and, over two weeks, refused to put a single concrete proposal on the table,” Eisenkot said in a statement. His wide-ranging camp has faced divisions over whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, the Arab-majority lists, or form a unity government with Likud. Netanyahu opponents scoffed at his offer of a rotating premiership. Youssef Jabareen, leader of the Arab-majority Joint List, which is expected to support an Eisenkot-led government without joining it, wrote: “The democratic majority has decided: this bloodstained, neglectful government must go. It is time to fulfill the shared will of the entire public, Jews and Arabs alike, and remove Netanyahu this (upcoming) week.” “Netanyahu’s proposal is yet another transparent con by a serial fraudster who has deceived every partner and violated every agreement,” wrote former premier Yair Lapid, co-chair of the centrist Beyachad party. Eisenkot’s Yashar party has so far agreed coalition deals with the left-leaning Democrats and the right-wing Israel Beiteinu party. Together, they have a combined total of 36 lawmakers — far short of the 61 needed for a majority in Israel’s 120-seat parliament. Israeli media reported that Mansour Abbas, the leader of the second Arab-Israeli party, Raam, is expected on Saturday to recognise Hamas as a “terror group” — a move that could pave the way for his party to join a possible Eisenkot-led coalition. But some of Eisenkot’s allies have voiced opposition to relying on the support of the Arab-majority lists, which made unprecedented gains in the election. The council said rather than explain what the Tinubu administration had done to ease the rising cost of living, Shettima had chosen to attack the opposition. ADC challenged him to account for the soaring prices of food, transportation and electricity. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, on Saturday, the council questioned Shettima’s influence in government and accused him of failing to make a meaningful contribution to decisions affecting the lives of ordinary Nigerians. “Vice President Kashim Shettima has reduced his role in this election to that of Tinubu’s campaign mascot: he appears at rallies to mock Atiku Abubakar, but disappears when Nigerians ask why food, transport and electricity have become so expensive,” it said. The campaign council recalled Shettima’s description of former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo as an “ice cream seller” during the 2023 election campaign, challenging him to show what he had achieved nearly four years into the Tinubu administration. “For the holder of Nigeria’s second-highest office, his contribution to the decisions shaping ordinary lives has been remarkably hard to see,” the statement added. It also questioned Shettima’s standing within the administration, alleging that the President’s wife, his son, Seyi Tinubu, the Chief of Staff and FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, wielded greater influence and commanded more attention than the Vice President. On Shettima’s suggestion that Atiku’s presidential ambition was driven by regional interests, the council insisted that the former Vice President’s campaign had a national appeal, pointing to his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, who hails from the South. “Atiku has taken his Affordable Life message to voters across Nigeria and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, is from the South. Nigerians facing the same hardship across the country do not need Tinubu’s campaign mascot to sort them into regional boxes,” it said. The council also demanded evidence for Shettima’s allegation that Atiku was seeking the presidency to “make money and foment mischief”, describing the accusation as baseless and unbecoming of a holder of the office of Vice President. “Let him produce a shred of evidence or withdraw it. His office does not turn a malicious invention into a fact,” the statement said. item.title: Kano deploys forest guards to tackle banditry, kidnapping
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government has deployed newly trained National Forest Guards to tackle banditry, kidnapping, and other security threats, particularly in communities bordering Kaduna and Katsina states. Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf announced this on Saturday during the passing-out parade of the first batch of 1,000 National Forest Guards held at the Kano State Corporate Security Institute, Zakirai, Gabasawa Local Government Area. Yusuf said the initiative was introduced to strengthen security in vulnerable communities and protect forests that could be used as hideouts by criminals. “Insecurity has increasingly become a challenge in some communities across Kano State, particularly those bordering neighbouring states such as Kaduna and Katsina, which have experienced security challenges, including banditry and kidnapping,” Yusuf said. “In our collective efforts to address this menace, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, through the Office of the National Security Adviser, graciously extended this important initiative to Kano State by approving the establishment of the National Forest Guards to complement the existing security architecture,” he added. According to him, the initiative will improve security operations, strengthen intelligence gathering at the grassroots, and protect rural communities. “The establishment and training of the National Forest Guards represent a step towards securing our forests, protecting vulnerable communities, and enhancing intelligence gathering at the grassroots level.” Yusuf urged the graduating guards to work closely with conventional security agencies, gather credible intelligence, and support lawful security operations. He also warned them against abusing their responsibilities. The governor further urged them to uphold discipline, integrity, professionalism, and respect for the rule of law. “You are expected to serve as vigilant guardians of our forests and rural communities. You must work hand in hand with established security agencies, gather credible intelligence, support lawful operations, and contribute positively to maintaining peace and order,” he said. He listed the establishment of the Anti-Phone Snatching Squad, the Kano State Security Neighbourhood Watch Corps, and the Multi-Agency Taskforce on Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking as some of the measures taken by his government to address insecurity. The governor called on residents, traditional rulers, religious leaders, and community groups to cooperate with the Forest Guards, stressing that security was a shared responsibility. “We are committed to supporting security agencies through financial and other forms of assistance,” he added. item.title: Ex-Lagos deputy gov, Senator Adebule, dies at 56
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State deputy governor and incumbent senator representing Lagos West senatorial district, Dr. Idiat Oluranti Adebule has died barely 24 hours after celebrating her 56th birthday in the state. Adebule, who was seeking re-election for a second term in the Senate, died in the early hours of Saturday. She was pronounced dead by medical experts at a private hospital in Ikeja, G.R.A., Ikeja Local Government Area of the state, where she was admitted after a brief illness. Adebule was said to be battling an undisclosed ailment for several years before she finally succumbed to death on Saturday. She was the deputy to former Governor Akinwunmi Ambode. The Lagos State All Progressives Congress, APC, spokesman, Seye Oladejo, confirmed the death. He described it as “a rude shock.” He prayed the Almighty God forgive her sins and grant her family, friends, and well-wishers the fortitude to bear the irreparable loss. He, however, announced the postponement of the earlier planned Lagos West senatorial campaign rally scheduled for next Monday, November 30. It was learned Senator Adebule was already preparing to attend the campaign rally scheduled for Police College, Ikeja, when the tragedy suddenly occurred. Tinubu mourns Reacting, President Bola Tinubu expressed “profound shock and sadness”. ‎President Tinubu described her death as a painful loss not only to Lagos State and the National Assembly, but to the nation as a whole, particularly at a time when her experience, commitment, and contributions to public service are needed. Tinubu extended his heartfelt condolences to her immediate family, the government and people of Lagos State, political associates, members of the All Progressives Congress (APC), the National Assembly, and all those mourning her passing. Lagos APC Meanwhile, in honour of the late lawmaker, the Director-General of the Lagos State APC PBAT/KOH Campaign Council, Senator Musiliu Obanikoro, has ordered the immediate suspension of all campaign activities across the state until further notice. ​Describing Senator Adebule’s passing as “a painful and irreplaceable loss,” the party noted that halting campaign operations reflects the profound grief within its ranks and the need to accord the late educationist and public servant a dignified farewell. ​”Her years of service, commitment to the progressive ideals of the APC and contributions to the political and developmental advancement of Lagos State will remain indelible,” the statement read. ​The party leadership has also directed all campaign structures, directorates, committees, and supporters to strictly comply with the suspension directive while calling on stakeholders and elected representatives to turn out to pay their final respects on Sunday. ​The Lagos APC also extended its condolences to Senator Adebule’s immediate family, political associates, and the constituents of Lagos West, praying for the peaceful repose of her soul. item.title: Man Utd thrashed 4-0 by Brentford in Pochettino’s home debut
item.description: Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 at home by Brentford on Mauricio Pochettino’s first home match in charge to leave the 20-time English champions still rooted in the Premier League relegation zone. Callum Wilson struck a first-half double before late goals from Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade sealed Brentford’s first win at Old Trafford for 89 years on Saturday. Pochettino replaced the sacked Michael Carrick earlier this month, tasked with turning around the fortunes of a club in steep decline. However, the Argentine could barely have imagined a worst start after also losing 4-0 away to Liverpool in his first match in charge last weekend. For the first time in 65 years, United have conceded four goals in three consecutive league matches. That shocking defensive record has plunged the Red Devils into a battle for survival. Only Crystal Palace sit below United and Pochettino’s men could slip to the foot of the table if the Eagles beat Hull on Sunday. Pochettino came out fighting after a series of refereeing decisions went against his side against Liverpool and in a controversial 2-2 draw at Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday. But there was no hiding place for the new boss or his players after their latest embarrassment. Brentford were missing first-choice striker Igor Thiago through suspension, but it mattered little as his deputy Wilson took advantage of United’s disorganised defence. An encouraging start by the home side was quickly forgotten when Wilson lashed home a brilliant finish to open the scoring on 19 minutes. The former Newcastle and West Ham striker then doubled his tally from Dango Ouattara’s pass 13 minutes later. The end of Carrick’s reign was marked by brief flickers of United resistance in comebacks to beat Roma and salvage a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. Youri Tielemans smashed against the crossbar as United pressed for a route back into the game in the second half. But their inability to defend ended any hope of a fightback as Ajer was given way too much space to fire in from a corner. Schade then completed the rout in stoppage time as Brentford climbed to fifth and within one point of the top four. item.title: Low turnout mars INEC mock polls in Bauchi
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on Saturday recorded low turnout of voters during its mock accreditation exercise conducted in selected polling units in Bauchi Local Government Area of Bauchi State ahead of the 2027 general elections. The exercise, aimed at testing the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, ahead of the elections, witnessed poor participation in some polling units visited by Vanguard. At Bakari Dukur Primary School polling unit, Vanguard observed that only a handful of voters were present, with fewer than five people seen waiting to undergo the accreditation process as INEC officials prepared for the exercise. A similar situation was observed at Yelwa Maternity Ward polling unit, where only a few voters turned out to participate in the exercise. Vanguard also observed that some voters encountered difficulties with the BVAS machines during the capturing of their information, while others arrived late, attributing their delay to the sanitation exercise observed by the state. However, the situation was slightly different at Makama/Sarki Baki polling units, where turnout was relatively fair, although some voters also arrived late. An INEC official at the polling unit attributed the late arrival of voters to the sanitation exercise, which affected their movement to the polling centres. An APC agent and observer at Makama, Yakubu Abduhamid, said poor awareness about the mock accreditation exercise contributed to the low turnout, noting that many residents appeared uninterested in the exercise. He, however, said those who participated at Sarki Baki polling unit conducted themselves peacefully, despite what he described as an unimpressive turnout. As of the time of filing this report, Vanguard had visited more than two polling units in Bauchi metropolis and observed that the exercise commenced late in some locations, while participation remained low. Some voters blamed the situation on inadequate awareness and the sanitation exercise, which they said hindered their timely arrival at the polling units. item.title: 2027; Yilwatda hands APC flags, brooms to Mbah, Nwifuru, Opah
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja National Chairman of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has presented the party’s flags and its symbolic broom to its governorship candidates in Enugu, Abia and Ebonyi states and told them to turn their campaigns into landslide victories in the 2027 general elections. The candidates are Peter Ndubuisi Mbah of Enugu State, Eric Chinemuecheya Opah of Abia State and Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru of Ebonyi State. In a statement by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, Yilwatda told the candidates to fly the party’s flag proudly in their states, carry its message to every community and constituency, and mobilise voters for resounding wins at the polls. The presentation took place on Friday at the APC presidential campaign rally in Enugu, led by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. Yilwatda made it through to Vice President Kashim Shettima in the presence of governors, members of the National Working Committee (NWC), elected officials and party stakeholders from across the country. He described the exercise as a demonstration of the party’s confidence in its candidates and its resolve to consolidate its strength across the federation. Yilwatda reserved his most emphatic charge for Nwifuru, the Ebonyi State Governor and APC governorship candidate, whom he urged to fly the party’s flag high and ensure that Ebonyi delivers an overwhelming harvest of votes for the APC. He told Opah, the party’s Abia governorship candidate, to take the flag across the state, deepen the party’s appeal at the grassroots and mobilise voters to deliver victory in the 2027 governorship election. Using the broom as an electoral metaphor, the National Chairman urged the candidates to make the most of every political opportunity to sweep votes for the APC on election day. He said the broom stands for more than the party’s identity. In his words as reported in the statement, it carries the party’s enduring message of unity, collective strength, political organisation and the determination to win through coordinated efforts. Yilwatda called on party leaders, members, supporters and grassroots mobilisers in the three states to close ranks and work together for the success of the candidates and the party’s wider electoral aspirations. He said the burden of winning elections does not rest on the candidates alone. Every party member, he said, has a role in strengthening the party’s structures, widening its support base and communicating the achievements and vision of the Tinubu administration. The National Chairman also pointed to President Tinubu’s leadership and the collective commitment of party stakeholders to consolidating the APC’s political dominance and delivering on its Renewed Hope Agenda. The Enugu rally, he said, gave the party another opportunity to show its organisational capacity, national reach and determination to approach the 2027 elections as a united political family. item.title: 2027 : Atiku, Obi relying on regional support to win election, Shettima says
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Vice President Kashim Shettima has accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi of relying on regional support in their bid to win the 2027 presidential election. Shettima made the remarks on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Enugu, where he questioned the opposition candidates’ campaign strategies and their efforts to build support across the country. He said Obi had visited 17 states, including all five states in the South-East and all South-South states except Rivers, but had made limited visits to other regions. According to Shettima, Obi had visited only Kaduna State in the North and Lagos State in the South-West. He also accused the Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate of attempting to use religious divisions to advance his political ambition, insisting that elections could not be won through division. “You cannot win election through divisions. We win elections through negotiation, through compromises, through bridge building,” the Vice-President said. Shettima also criticised Atiku’s campaign activities, claiming that the former vice-president had visited only six states and had not travelled to any state in Southern Nigeria. “My brother Atiku Abubakar, he has so far visited six states in the Federation. He has not visited one state in Southern Nigeria. He has concentrated purely in the North,” he said. The Vice-President argued that presidential candidates needed support beyond their traditional political strongholds to secure victory, citing former President Muhammadu Buhari’s eventual success after building an alliance with the South-West. He said Buhari’s support in the North alone had not been enough to secure the presidency until he formed an alliance with the South-West. Shettima expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would defeat the opposition candidates in the 2027 election. item.title: Poor turnout, smooth BVAS operation mark INEC mock polls in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) mock accreditation and voting exercise in selected polling units in Kebbi State on Saturday recorded low voter turnout, although the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines operated without reported malfunctions. The exercise witnessed a predominantly female turnout, with relatively few male voters seen at several polling units visited. At Aliero Housing Estate 006 Primary School polling unit, female voters turned out for accreditation, while only a few male voters were sighted. Security personnel, including officers of the Police, Department of State Services (DSS), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and State Security Service (SCIB), were deployed to provide security during the exercise. INEC ad hoc staff at the polling unit confirmed that the BVAS machines were functioning effectively during voter authentication. A visit to Gwadangaji 001 polling unit also showed a low turnout, with a few female voters presenting themselves for accreditation and no male voters sighted at the time. The voters were seen checking their names on the lists displayed on the walls before proceeding with the exercise. However, at Justice Ibrahim Umar polling unit in the GRA NEPA area, a relatively large number of female voters turned out for the mock exercise. The ad hoc staff confirmed that the two BVAS machines provided for the polling unit were working effectively, adding that no malfunction had been recorded since the exercise commenced at 9 a.m. Meanwhile, an APC stakeholder, Alhaji Abubakar ABK, described the exercise as impressive and peaceful. He attributed the participation of female voters to what he described as the humanitarian interventions of Governor Idris, expressing optimism that voters would turn out in large numbers during the January 2027 general elections. ABK urged voters to maintain the peaceful conduct witnessed during the mock exercise when participating in the main elections in 2027. item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Prince Adewole Adebayo, has urged Nigerians to vote out the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general election, saying the country’s future should be determined by its citizens rather than a privileged political group. Adebayo also called on Nigerians to move beyond complaints about bad governance and participate actively in the electoral process, insisting that voting remained the most effective democratic instrument for changing an administration. He spoke during an SDP town hall meeting with party leaders, candidates and supporters in Nasarawa State, where he criticised the APC over the economic and security challenges confronting the country. He said: “A bad government does not go by you abusing it. A bad government does not go by you shouting. A government goes by you voting it out. The government does not care whether you abuse it, but it cares whether you vote. So, you must vote.” The SDP candidate said the central question before Nigerians in 2027 was whether the country belonged to its citizens or a privileged group exercising political and economic influence. “What is at stake in 2027 is whether Nigeria belongs to the people or whether Nigeria belongs to the cabal. You must say with your mouth and tell your neighbours that Nigeria belongs to the Nigerian people,” he said. Adebayo said the SDP was offering Nigerians an alternative political and economic programme focused on tackling poverty, insecurity, unemployment and the rising cost of living. He said the party’s manifesto contained proposals aimed at improving citizens’ welfare and ensuring that public resources were directed towards addressing their most pressing needs. On the economy, he promised that an SDP administration would reduce the pump price of petrol to N200 per litre without fuel subsidy, arguing that this would be achievable through measures to eliminate corruption and improve efficiency in the petroleum sector. “We will give you petrol for N200 per litre without subsidy. We will sell it for N200, and NNPC will still make a profit because we will stop funding corruption,” he said. He promised that an SDP government would implement policies to make food affordable and ensure Nigerians had access to basic necessities. item.title: [PHOTOS] Moment Voter Makes Frustrating Facial Expressions While Being Captured On INEC’s BVAS
item.description: A voter at polling unit 001 in Barnawa, Kaduna South Local Government Area, captured attention on Saturday, as she made different frustrating facial expressions while being captured on the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) during the INEC’s mock accreditation exercise in Kaduna State. Our correspondent, who monitored the exercise, noted that a voter spent more than five minutes completing the accreditation and voting process due to network challenges affecting the machine. The exercise is expected to simulate the Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Meanwhile, one of the voters at polling unit 002, Narayi Primary School, in Kaduna State, Rebecca Oladipo, has expressed frustration over the absence of the Independent National Electoral Commission’s officials at the mock accreditation on Saturday. Oladipo, who said she arrived at the polling unit for the INEC mock accreditation exercise at 10:30 am, questioned the commission’s preparedness to conduct a credible election in 2027, expressing concern that the mock election, which is expected to test INEC’s operational readiness, appears to be starting on a shaky note. According to her, the delay left those who turned up for the exercise waiting without knowing when the exercise would commence. Rebecca Oladipo “I’m here at Narayi Primary School, one of the wards chosen for the mock exercise. I have been here for the past two hours. INEC is supposed to start the exercise at 8:30. Now we are at around 10:30, and we are yet to see them. “This is really disheartening because a lot of people have been here. Security agencies have been here; even I came to meet them here. One or two voters have been here, and they left. “I’m using this opportunity to say to INEC that we in Narayi ward are not happy because we heard that other wards have started the exercises, so we should not be left behind. “I’m using this opportunity to tell INEC that in the main election, please, please, let it not be like this. It has always been like this in the previous elections. Maybe because Narayi people are good and kind people. item.title: PHOTOS: Low Turnout as INEC begins Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) commenced its mock elections in Borno State to test-run voting equipment and logistical readiness ahead of the 2027 general elections. However, the exercise recorded a low voter turnout in some polling units visited by our correspondent due to what many residents described as “a lack of awareness”. The exercise, designed to evaluate the deployment of election personnel and the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) across all 27 local government areas of the state, also faced a slow start in some polling units. Across Jere and Maiduguri Metropolitan Councils security personnel, including police officers and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and Road Safety Officials, were present early at some polling units, INEC officials arrived late. Yul recalls Pete Edochie’s final moments 3 killed, many injured as rival youth groups clash in Cross River At the Bulama Jidda polling unit in Gomari Airport, voting commenced at 8:44 a.m. after officials arrived, slightly behind schedule. However, poll workers and voters at the station confirmed that the BVAS machines functioned efficiently. “There is actually a low turnout, but the use of BVAS is smooth. At some point, we are using it offline, but will upload it when we reach areas with a robust network,” one polling unit officer stated. Interviews with residents across various areas revealed that public awareness of the exercise was generally poor, with many locals unaware that the mock election was taking place. At the Gwange III polling unit, turnout was similarly low. Some prospective voters said they encountered some technical hitches during accreditation, reporting that the BVAS failed to capture their fingerprints and facial features. Speaking on condition of anonymity, an Ad-hoc staff, noted that affected individuals were not issued ballot papers. Instead, their details were compiled for INEC to review and resolve prior to the general elections. At the Government House polling unit (Unit 001, Maisandari Ward), where voter turnout was notably impressive, the process ran without hitches. Abacha Anas, the Electoral Officer for Operations for INEC in the Maiduguri Metropolitan Council, described the exercise as smooth and successful.
